entries.notes:
Too close to original, reduce strength
REBUILD ROUND 2: user on r1 — 'strength too high, too close to the original'. 80 -> 60, PROMPT HELD IDENTICAL so strength is the only variable. Note 80 was the value that read as correct roster proportions, so the useful band for this entry is narrow: below ~50 expect the vagrant's green/brown palette and body plan to stop being enforced at all (at frame level, 70 was already where faces started appearing). If 60 reads proportionally right but still not spectral enough, the NEXT lever is contrast, not strength and not more description: desaturate the cloth so the rim glow and mist hem are the only saturated elements ('colourless grey cloth, the only colour is the pale blue glow'). Contrast is what sells spectral at 64px.
REBUILD ROUND 3: user — 'still not good, we need to move further away. Shift the colour scheme to black, grey and white for this one.' Two user-directed changes: strength 60 -> 45 (further from the vagrant's body plan and palette) and a hard MONOCHROME palette. The r2 experiment was informative: holding the prompt fixed while dropping 80 -> 60 proved that lower strength buys PALETTE FREEDOM, NOT SPECTRALNESS — the set went bluer, not ghostlier. The spectral read was never losing to chain strength; it was losing because everything in the sprite was equally coloured, so a glow had nothing to stand out against. Monochrome cloth fixes that for free: with no colour anywhere else, the white rim glow and mist hem become the only luminous elements. Contrast sells 'spectral' at 64px; description never has. WATCH AT 45: the vagrant's body plan is only weakly enforced this low — check roster proportions first, and if the build drifts, come back up to ~55 rather than adding proportion words.

entries.notes:
BALANCED = mid grey, detailed garment, settled form. The class's neutral body and the reference the other two depart from.
Stage 2 Spirit frame — WHITE / GREY / BLACK VALUE RAMP (user's idea, 2026-07-25): light = white, balanced = grey, heavy = black, on the rebuilt monochrome root. Value contrast is the most legible signal at 64px — far stronger than shape detail, which is what failed in rounds 1-3 — and it maps onto the density axis (white = barely materialised, black = dense and almost physical) while keeping all three unmistakably one family. Garment axis from the user still applies underneath: plain tunic -> detailed tunic -> armour worked into the tunic.
LEGIBILITY GUARD (deliberate, do not strip): the player body must stay readable on all eleven biomes. User on r9: 'a complete miss, the style was completely off the mark' (candidates came back bulky, spacesuit-like, desaturated to blue/purple, one with a weapon shape). ROOT CAUSE: PROMPT BLOAT. Across rounds 7-9 this prompt grew to ~120 words juggling mask lighting + explicit rotation geometry + head-size proportions, while EVERY accepted root in this manifest uses a SHORT identity-only prompt with style carried by the params and the chain. The extra instruction crowded out the style. This round returns to the proven shape: short identity prompt, one brief framing clause (as the classless entry has) instead of the rotation paragraph, no head-size clause, initImageStrength back to 70 (the value that held style best across the whole roster). GENERAL RULE FOR THIS CATEGORY: when a player entry drifts off-style, SHORTEN the prompt before adding anything to it — accumulated fixes are themselves a failure mode. Fix proportions with the deterministic retouch script, not with more prompt words. ROUND 11 — PERSPECTIVE, ROOT CAUSE FOUND. User: the accepted r10 sprite is 'almost right but the face is turned toward the camera where it should face right'. DIAGNOSIS: a FEATURELESS OVAL MASK CARRIES NO FACING INFORMATION. Every other class signals its turn through head geometry (hood cavity, angled helm front, the Slinger's painted eye); a blank oval has no front, so the head defaults to face-on however hard the prompt pushes 'south-east' — which is why this entry alone kept regressing on perspective while the Squire's helm fix held. TWO CHANGES: (1) initImage switched from classless.png to cadence.png @ 90 — an initImage asserts structure that negatives cannot outvote, which has been the enemy all session; here it is the TOOL, because the accepted Striker already has exactly the 3/4 turn we want, so it asserts the pose while the prompt supplies the red robe and mask. Watch for Striker identity bleed (grey/brown palette, shoulder guards) and drop toward 70 if it shows. (2) The mask is now described with a front: offset toward the right of the head, seen at a three-quarter angle, right edge lit and left side shaded, so it reads as a turned face rather than a flat disc; 'mask facing the viewer' and 'flat round mask' added as negatives. GENERAL RULE: chain from whichever accepted sibling already has the property you keep failing to get — the chain is a structure lever, not just a style lever.
